Decision Needed: Should a Quality Manager who is not an administrator still be able to place a lot on hold and release a hold, or is that also administrator-only?
Options Discussed: A) Hold / un-hold stays with the Quality Manager (and administrators), everything else administrator-only / B) Everything, including hold, administrator-only / C) Hold also open to a Production Manager
Recommendation (Claude): A. Putting a lot on hold is a safety action that should not wait for an administrator; it is still logged with who, when and the reason, and every other lot change stays administrator-only. B would stop a Quality Manager quarantining suspect material unless they are also an administrator.
Decision: Not needed: KW-87 is withdrawn. Lot supplier lot / expiry correction already works for administrators (Lots > Trace > Correct details), so the hold question does not arise.

Decision Needed: How should a renamed container keep its old name in existing records: keep the stored text and resolve the old name through an alias, or move the stored references to item ids and rebaseline the signed production-log hashes?
Options Discussed: A) Keep stored text as written; resolve the old name through the alias for lookups (no change to signed records) / B) Replace the stored name text with item ids and rebaseline (one source of truth, but the signed snapshots change and need a version bump and re-hash)
Recommendation (Claude): A. A finished record should keep what it said at the time (lot numbers on the IBCs are text anyway), the release hashes stay valid, and the change is small and testable. B is cleaner in theory but rewrites the packaging rows of signed logs.
Decision: A: keep the stored text in existing records as written and resolve an old name through the alias; new entries use the new name; signed release hashes stay valid.
